chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Indeed, let not one of you lie down fully reclined in the bathhouse, for it melts the fat of the kidneys, and let him not rub his feet with the clay/rough stone, for it causes leprosy.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْخَزَف: Clay / Rough stone used for scrubbing

ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits and risks of practices in the bathhouse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical medical wisdom of the Imams, linking specific bathhouse habits to physiological health; lying down fully reclined was believed to affect kidney function, while vigorous scrubbing with rough materials was associated with skin diseases like leprosy (judham). It reflects the Shia tradition of integrating spiritual purity with physical well-being, emphasizing preventive care in daily hygiene practices.
